title: A summary before the weekend
author: AdventurousHat8741
selftext:
Core Indicators and Logic Analysis of the Strategy Chart:

Main Chart Area (Top): Double Exponential Moving Averages (EMA)

20 EMA (Orange Dashed Line - Tactical Fast Line): Captures strong trends. When the price consistently stays above the 20 EMA, it indicates extremely strong momentum (such as the surge in your screenshot), indicating a hold/observation zone

50 EMA (Green Solid Line - Strategic Bottom Line): A medium-term trend indicator.

Key Signal Points:

Golden Cross: The 20 EMA crosses above the 50 EMA, confirming a major upward wave and serving as a right-side entry signal

Support Pullback: Strong trending stocks rarely fall below the 50 EMA. When the price retraces to near the 20 or 50 EMA, stabilizes, and forms a bullish candlestick, it is usually an excellent entry/add-to-position point

Trailing Stop (Trip Stop/Take Profit): Holding onto 3x leveraged (TQQQ) or high-growth tech stocks (SMCI) is strictly prohibited. Once the price closes below the 20 EMA or even the 50 EMA, a right-side stop-loss or phased liquidation must be initiated to prevent significant profit retracement.

Sub-chart area (below): RSI (Relative Strength Index) (14)

Overbought (>70, Red Zone): Entering the extreme overbought zone. Although high-momentum stocks may remain in the red zone for a long time, it is not advisable to blindly chase the price higher. A phased reduction strategy can be used instead

Oversold (<30, Green Zone): Entering the oversold zone. Since TQQQ is anchored to the Nasdaq 100 index, it inherently possesses long-term upward defensive value. Therefore, when the RSI reaches 30 or even lower, it is usually an excellent opportunity for phased pyramid-style buying

The above content is merely a sharing of my personal research and insights on quantitative technical indicator strategies
